## How the forecast is made {#methods}

This section describes the data, the personas, the questions put to the models and how the answers become a forecast.

### Data

The data come from the Cooperative Election Study [@ces2024; @ces2025], the polls listed on Wikipedia, and past governor results.

```{=html}
<details class="more"><summary>Show the polls by state</summary>
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-polls
#| tbl-cap: "Polls used in the forecast, by state, with fieldwork ending on or after 1 August 2026. Likely voters is the share of those polls that report a likely-voter sample. The average weights each poll by its sample size and by how recent it is (half weight for a poll a month older)."
P.tbl_polls()
```

```{=html}
</details>
```

### Personas and the weighting frame

Each state's AI survey uses 100 personas built from real survey respondents, weighted to match the state's voters.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-composition
#| tbl-cap: "The 3,600 personas against the weighted frame they are weighted to, averaged over the 36 states. The frame counts every eligible CES respondent with their survey weight; the personas count each person once."
P.tbl_composition()
```

```{=html}
<details class="more"><summary>Show the frame for each state</summary>
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-frame
#| tbl-cap: "The weighting frame by state, smallest effective sample first. The effective sample is the number of unweighted respondents that would give the same precision; the last two columns compare the 2024 and 2025 surveys, which the frame pools."
P.tbl_frame_states()
```

```{=html}
</details>
```

### Asking the models

Three language models from three companies answered as each persona.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-models
#| tbl-cap: "The three models, how they were called, and the share of all their answers (every method, every day) that could be used."
P.tbl_models()
```

```{=html}
<details class="more"><summary>Show the exact prompt one persona received, and the reply</summary>
```

```{python}
P.example_prompt()
```

```{=html}
</details>
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-responses
#| tbl-cap: "Method A answers to the governor question by model, over three repeats of all 3,600 personas. Independent or third party counts named candidates such as Ken Block in Rhode Island; Other is the model writing in someone not listed; Unusable answers failed the format checks even after a retry."
P.tbl_response_distribution()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ticket
#| tbl-cap: "Ticket splitting in Method A: the share of personas who chose a major-party candidate for governor and the other party for the House."
P.tbl_ticket_splitting()
```

### Combining the sources and simulating the election

The corrected AI surveys, the polls and past results are blended, and the election is simulated 10,000 times.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-fundamentals
#| tbl-cap: "The past-results regression: the Democratic margin in the 2014, 2018 and 2022 governor races on state lean, incumbency and the president's party."
P.tbl_fundamentals()
```
